extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Department of Education federal financial assistance (elementary/secondary/postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, compliance officers, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Final regulations (34 CFR 106) implementing Title IX that set definitions, recipient obligations, grievance-procedure standards, supportive measures, trainings, recordkeeping, scope (including sexual orientation/gender identity and pregnancy), and enforcement expectations for education programs or activities receiving federal funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.1 Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose of the regulations: clarify scope and application of Title IX and obligations of recipients to provide an educational environment free from discrimination on the basis of sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets regulatory intent to align Title IX requirements with nondiscrimination mandate and allow recipients discretion to account for variations in size, population, and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.2 Definition of 'Administrative Law Judge'
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the term 'Administrative Law Judge' for purposes of the Part 106 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.2 Definition of 'Complainant'
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'Complainant' (the person alleged to be the victim of conduct that could constitute sex discrimination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.2 Definition of 'Complaint'
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'Complaint' (a report or allegation submitted under the recipient's grievance procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes discussion of rights of respondents and complainants, effect on recipients, and whether to broaden definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.2 Definition of 'Disciplinary Sanctions'
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the term 'Disciplinary Sanctions' used in grievance and discipline provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.2 Definitions of 'Elementary School' and 'Secondary School'
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines what constitutes elementary and secondary schools under these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.2 Definition of 'Postsecondary Institution'
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'Postsecondary Institution' for application of Part 106 requirements specific to higher education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.2 Definition of Prohibited 'Sex-Based Harassment'
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'Sex-Based Harassment' including quid pro quo and hostile environment forms; includes sub-criteria (Davis standard; severe or pervasive; subjective/objective offense) and scope (online harassment, sex stereotyping, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains data related to sex-based harassment, burden and cost considerations, vagueness/overbreadth concerns, First Amendment intersections, application in elementary/secondary/postsecondary contexts, and specific offenses (sexual assault, consent, dating/domestic violence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.2 Definition of 'Relevant'
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'Relevant' evidence or information for grievance/investigation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.2 Definition of 'Remedies'
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'Remedies' that may be provided to a complainant if sex discrimination is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.2 Definition of 'Respondent'
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'Respondent' (the person alleged to have committed sex discrimination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.2 Definition of 'Student With a Disability'
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines protections and status of students with disabilities under the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intersects with access to accommodations and auxiliary aids; coverage in postsecondary settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.2 Definition of 'Title IX'
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the statutory scope and meaning of 'Title IX' as used in the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Definitions (Section 106.2) — 'Employee', 'Federal Financial Assistance', 'Program or Activity', 'Recipient', 'Student', 'Party', 'Sex Discrimination'
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of other foundational terms used throughout the rule, including proposed additions (e.g., 'Party', 'Sex Discrimination').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies which entities and activities are covered and interactions with related statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.11 Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets the application rules for Title IX (what programs/activities are covered, obligations to address conduct occurring under recipient's education program or activity, extraterritorial application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses conduct in buildings owned/controlled by student organizations, conduct under recipient's disciplinary authority, benefits and burdens for recipients, and intersections with free speech and ministerial exception doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.6(e) Interaction Between Title IX and FERPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains the effect of FERPA and GEPA on Title IX obligations, particularly disclosure of information relevant to allegations of sex discrimination and types of recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses interplay by recipient type and issues for students with disabilities, sexual orientation/gender identity, and pregnancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.6(g) Exercise of Rights by Parents or Legal Representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses how parents, guardians, or authorized legal representatives may exercise rights under Title IX on behalf of protected individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.6(b) Preemptive Effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes preemptive effect of Title IX in relation to other laws or requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.8(a) Designation of a Title IX Coordinator
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must designate a Title IX Coordinator responsible for coordinating compliance and responses to sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinator role scope, prompt/effective action, Title IX Coordinator-initiated complaints, duty to monitor, and comprehensive coordinator requirements discussed elsewhere (106.44(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.8(b) and (c) Nondiscrimination Policy, Grievance Procedures, and Notice of Nondiscrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must adopt and publish a nondiscrimination policy, grievance procedures, and provide notice of nondiscrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations include requests to add protected bases, additional information in procedures/notice, publication requirements, and free speech/religious exemption concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.8(d) Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide training related to Title IX obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers benefits/time/expense of training, frequency, impartiality, topics (definition of sex-based harassment, notification requirements, supportive measures), individuals to be trained, and live trainings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.8(e) Students With Disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Special requirements and considerations to ensure students with disabilities have access to Title IX protections and accommodations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access to accommodations/auxiliary aids; postsecondary-specific concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.8(f) Recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordkeeping obligations for recipients, including documentation records, training materials, and pregnancy-related records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies types of records to retain and addresses privacy/FERPA intersections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.44(a) Recipients' Duty To Address Sex Discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: General duty of recipients to respond to and address sex discrimination within their programs or activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes notice requirements, liability standard comparisons, neutrality/impartiality expectations for coordinators, and impact on dual enrollment programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.44(b) Monitoring for Barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must monitor for barriers to reporting and participation that may impede Title IX enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses reporting channels, free speech and academic freedom, and compliance burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.44(c) Notification Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for notifying individuals about sex discrimination and information related to complaints (e.g., how to report, safety threats, study abroad implications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses consistency with state laws, disclosure scope, employee complainants, law enforcement interface, age-appropriateness, and training on notification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections 106.2 and 106.44(d) 'Confidential Employee' Requirements and Definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines categories of 'confidential employee' and duties: privileged communications, designated service providers, IRB-approved researchers, and recipient's duty to identify confidential employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets confidentiality limits, interaction with grievance procedures, and requirements for identifying confidential employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.44(e) Public Awareness Events
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing public awareness events related to sex discrimination and Title IX compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.44(f) Title IX Coordinator Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive requirements and scope for the Title IX Coordinator role, including responsibilities to take prompt and effective action and monitoring duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses coordinator-initiated complaints, steps to prevent recurrence, prompt remedying obligations, and proposed regulatory text for coordinator duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections 106.44(g) and 106.2 Supportive Measures and Definition of 'Supportive Measures'
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of supportive measures and recipient responsibility to offer and coordinate them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types of supportive measures, temporary supportive measures that impose burdens, challenges to supportive measures, disclosure rules, and considerations for students with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.44(h) Emergency Removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority and standards for emergency removal of individuals posing non-physical, serious, and imminent threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses interplay with protected speech, partial emergency removals, supportive measures alternatives, and other legal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.44(i) Administrative Leave
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and use of administrative leave for employee respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.44(j) Prohibited Disclosures of Personally Identifiable Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibitions on disclosing PII related to complainants/respondents and other privacy protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.44(k) Informal Resolution Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for offering and conducting informal resolution processes, including prohibition for certain student-employee pairings and requirements for consent, notice, facilitators, and agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains discretion to offer informal resolution, voluntariness, notice prior to resolution, facilitator qualifications, and limits on use (e.g., student complaints against employee respondents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Framework for Grievance Procedures — Due Process and Related Factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall framework for grievance procedures, including due process expectations, administrative burdens, bifurcation between students and employees, quasi-judicial appearance concerns, and consistency with other civil rights laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses how to determine what process is due, identifying relevant interests, bias issues, and application across elementary/secondary/postsecondary settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(b)(1) Treat Complainants and Respondents Equitably
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must treat complainants and respondents equitably throughout grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains equitable treatment expectations, trauma-informed approach, fairness, neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(b)(2) Conflicts of Interest or Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on conflicts of interest and bias in grievance processes and requirements for impartial decisionmakers/investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses single-investigator model concerns and structural safeguards to avoid bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(b)(3) Presumption of Non-Responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Presumption that respondent is not responsible until a determination is made at the conclusion of grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections 106.45(b)(4) and 106.46(e)(5) Timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to adopt and follow reasonable timeframes for grievance processes and notice of any delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes directed questions and commentary on appropriate timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(b)(5) Reasonable Limitations on Sharing of Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable limits on sharing allegations and investigation information with third parties to protect privacy and due process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses privacy protections, more stringent protections, due process concerns, authority and First Amendment implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(b)(6) Objective Evaluation of All Relevant Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement for objective evaluation of all relevant evidence by decisionmakers and investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes neutral assessment and avoidance of prejudgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(b)(7) Exclusion of Impermissible Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion of certain categories of evidence regardless of relevance (privileged evidence, treatment records, evidence of sexual interests or prior sexual conduct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subparts specify privileged evidence or communications with confidential employees, treatment records, and limits on sexual history evidence (including evidence offered to prove consent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(c) Notice of Allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for providing written notice of allegations to parties, including content and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(d) Dismissal of a Complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds and procedures for permissive dismissals (unable to identify respondent; respondent not participating/is not employed by recipient; complainant withdraws; alleged conduct would not constitute sex discrimination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes notification of dismissal, appeal rights, and prompt/effective steps after dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(e) Consolidation of Complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and limits for consolidating multiple complaints into a single proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses consolidation when parties are opposing, constitutional concerns, and FERPA implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(f) Complaint Investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigation procedures including burden allocation, opportunity to present witnesses and relevant evidence, review and determination of relevant evidence, and access to evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details investigative burden on recipients, equal opportunity to access evidence, reasonable opportunity to respond, and safeguards against unauthorized disclosures; includes FERPA considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(f)(1) Investigative Burden on Recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients bear the burden of investigating allegations once a complaint is filed (scope and standard of investigative effort).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(f)(2) Opportunity To Present Witnesses and Other Relevant Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must have opportunity to present witnesses and evidence that are relevant and not otherwise impermissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(f)(4) Access to the Relevant and Not Otherwise Impermissible Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must have equal opportunity to access evidence or accurate descriptions of evidence, reasonable opportunity to respond, and protections against unauthorized disclosures; interactions with FERPA noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections specify (i) equal access, (ii) reasonable opportunity to respond, (iii) unauthorized disclosures, and related FERPA issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(g) Evaluating Allegations and Assessing Credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for how investigators/decisionmakers evaluate allegations and assess credibility of parties and witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses methods for assessing credibility and factors to consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(h)(1) Standard of Proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses the standard of proof to be used in determinations (and related directed questions about standards and comparability across proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses options and whether different standards may apply to students vs employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(h)(2) Notification of Determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for notifying parties of the determination whether sex discrimination occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(h)(3) Remedies and Prompt/Effective Steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Duty to provide remedies to complainants and other appropriate prompt and effective steps when discrimination is found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Range of remedies and requirement to act before imposing disciplinary sanctions (see 106.45(h)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(h)(4) Compliance Before Imposition of Disciplinary Sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with grievance and procedural provisions before imposing disciplinary sanctions based on a determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(h)(5) Prohibition on Discipline Based Solely on Determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on imposing discipline solely on the basis of the determination; addresses false statements and consensual sexual activity considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(i) Appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for allowing appeals of determinations, including permitted bases and procedural requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses grounds for appeal and related procedural fairness concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(l) Range of Supportive Measures and Disciplinary Sanctions and Remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissible range of supportive measures and disciplinary sanctions and remedies that may be employed by recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.46 — Grievance Procedures Specific to Postsecondary Institutions (Student Complainant or Student Respondent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional procedural protections and rules specific to postsecondary contexts, including written notice, in-advance notice of meetings, advisor role, access to evidence, live questioning, and live hearings considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes student-employee considerations, advisor choice and restrictions, expert witnesses, timeframes, access to investigative reports, cross-examination/advisors-of-choice issues, and logistics of live hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.46(e)(2) Role of Advisor
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies advisor rights and limitations, including choice of advisor, restrictions on participation, and advisor conduct during proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses advisor participation limits and institutional obligations regarding advisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.46(f)(1-4) Procedures for Questioning Parties and Witnesses; Live-Questioning; Assessment of Credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and standards for questioning, including whether and how live questioning or cross-examination occurs, decisionmaker evaluation of questions, and potential inferences for refusal to answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses methods for assessing credibility, due process concerns, Mathews balancing test, and logistics/recording issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.46(g) Live Hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of live hearings: impacts, fairness concerns, removal of live hearing requirement, and when live hearings may be required; logistics if used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores benefits and burdens of live hearings on parties and institutions and alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.46(h) Determination Whether Sex-Based Harassment Occurred
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and procedures for the decisionmaker's determination in postsecondary sex-based harassment cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.46(i) Appeals (Postsecondary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals processes as applied at postsecondary institutions, including requests to add or modify bases for appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.46(j) Informal Resolution (Postsecondary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissible use and limitations of informal resolution mechanisms in postsecondary settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.47 Assistant Secretary Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Process and standards for Assistant Secretary review of determinations in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy and Parental Status — Revised Definitions (Section 106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'Pregnancy or Related Conditions' and 'Parental Status' and scope of coverage (including termination of pregnancy, abortion neutrality, and state law interactions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses admissions, reasonable modifications, lactation spaces, voluntary leaves, comparable treatment to other temporary medical conditions, limitations on supporting documentation, and other implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.40 — Discrimination Based on Pregnancy and Parental Status (Students)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligations to prevent discrimination against students based on parental/family/marital status and pregnancy-related conditions, including notification, reasonable modifications, leaves of absence, lactation space, and comparable treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes process for providing modifications, Title IX Coordinator role, timelines, interaction with disability law, and certification requirements to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections 106.51 & 106.57 — Employment Protections for Pregnancy/Parental Status
rubrics_metrics.description: Protections for employees re: granting/return from leaves, parental/family/marital status, lactation time and space, voluntary leaves, and comparable treatment to other medical conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses pre-employment inquiries and implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.10 Scope of Title IX Coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the scope of sex discrimination covered under Title IX, including authority to regulate sexual orientation and gender identity, reliance on Bostock/Title VII, sex characteristics, sex stereotypes, pregnancy, and menstruation or related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses participation consistent with gender identity, de minimis harm standard, parental rights, intersections with health care and religion, appearance codes, and applicability across facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.31(a) Education Programs or Activities—General
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains what constitutes an education program or activity (de minimis harm standard, participation consistent with gender identity, parental rights, intersection with health care/religion, appearance codes, juvenile justice facilities, burden on schools).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.71 Retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits retaliation against persons for participation in protected activity under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses examples of prohibited retaliation, interaction with §106.45(h)(5), First Amendment implications, and requested clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.2 Definition of 'Retaliation' and 'Peer Retaliation'
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'Retaliation' (protected activity; adverse action; causal connection) and 'Peer Retaliation' in the Title IX context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outdated Regulatory Provisions — Sections to Remove or Update
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifies outdated provisions (self-evaluation, transition plans, adjustment period) to be revised or removed for clarity and modernization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscellaneous Provisions (Parental Rights, Religious Exemptions, Rulemaking Process, Comment Period, Effective Date/Retroactivity, Prevention, Federalism, Terminology, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various cross-cutting regulatory topics and clarifications: parental rights, religious exemptions (Sections 106.12(b)/(c)), transparency, rulemaking process, length of public comment period and process for submitting/posting comments, effective date and retroactivity, prevention strategies, Tenth Amendment concerns, authority limits, coordination, terminology, discipline of student organizations, contractors, data collection/climate surveys, OCR enforcement practices, severability, and comments outside Title IX scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides guidance on implementation, coordination with other laws, and agency positions on litigated or constitutional issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) — Cost/Benefit and Small Entity Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of the costs, benefits, baseline assumptions, population estimates, and Regulatory Flexibility Act (small entity) impacts of the final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes modeling approach, data sources, estimated changes in investigations, costs of training/recordkeeping/supportive measures, alternatives considered, and accounting statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling and Assumptions Underlying RIA (Specific Topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific RIA topics such as costs of training, recordkeeping, application of Title IX, duty to address sex discrimination, coordinator obligations, notification requirements, provision of supportive measures, impartial review, grievance procedures, training for decisionmakers, single-investigator model, pregnancy provisions, and scope expansions (menstruation, sexual orientation, gender identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details the Department's modeling choices, data limitations, and rationale for estimated impacts (including a 10% estimated increase in investigations due to clarity on sexual orientation/gender identity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and Public Inspection Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligations on recipients to maintain records and make certain materials available for public inspection consistent with Federal Register/public inspection rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to official PDF and XML versions and guidance to verify contents against official editions; includes record access and public inspection logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions Governing Scope of Remedies and Relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Parameters for remedial actions a recipient must take when discrimination is found, including measures to ensure access and to prevent recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes requirement to take prompt and effective steps and examples of remedial measures and supportive services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy, FERPA, and Information Sharing Constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Constraints on disclosure of information due to FERPA and other privacy laws when implementing Title IX obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses disclosure of evidence, interplay with grievance procedures, and exceptions where disclosure is permissible or required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-Investigator Model — Considerations and Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of the single-investigator model (investigator serving as decisionmaker) and concerns about bias and due process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes references in RIA and procedural framework and potential restrictions or mitigations (e.g., separation of investigation and decisionmaking).
